what: A 256-bit AVX-VNNI microkernel for the Q8_0 unified prefill owner. The owner's fast inner was gated on avx512f+avx512bw+avx512vnni, so every consumer Intel part from 12th gen onward -- which carries AVX-VNNI on 256-bit registers and has AVX-512 fused off -- fell back to the AVX2 maddubs+madd inner. Unlike the K-quant owner, THIS owner is default-on for windows x86_64, so the slow path was shipping.
lever: q8_0_packed_rows4_gemm4_accumulate_block_avxvnni, selected when the Q8 owner is on AND its VNNI flag is on AND avx512vnni is absent AND avxvnni+avx2 are present. Additive: the AVX-512 4x4 path, the AVX-512 4x8 path, the AVX2 path and the scalar path are byte-identical to main.

host.cpu: win i9-14900HX 8P+16E (24 physical / 32 logical), Raptor Lake
host.isa: avx2=true fma=true avxvnni=true; avx512f=false avx512bw=false avx512vnni=false
host.why_this_host_matters: It is the shape the old gate misses: VNNI dot-product instructions present, AVX-512 absent. On this class of part the default-on Q8 owner was permanently on its slowest vector inner.
host.gpu: RTX 4060 Laptop present but hidden with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 for every measurement
host.power: AC for every reported number (Win32_Battery BatteryStatus=2 recorded pre and post each run)

method.pairing: all three arms run once per round inside one process, interleaved, so a per-round ratio cancels thermal and clock drift. 2 warmup rounds discarded.
method.statistic: median of per-round ratios, 95% percentile bootstrap CI over rounds (2000 resamples)
method.engagement_check: every row carries owner_prefill_taken and q8_avxvnni256_taken; the sweep hard-fails a config whose owner never dispatched.
method.harness_fix_required_first: The Q8 sweep hard-coded owner_vnni4x4 / owner_vnni4x8 arms with no capability branch. On a host without AVX-512 those arms set the VNNI env, got use_vnni=false, and silently measured the AVX2 inner against itself -- a fake null. The sweep now picks the 512-bit arms only when avx512f/bw/vnni are present and otherwise measures owner_avxvnni256 under a label that says which kernel actually ran.

primary.baseline: owner_avx2 -- the arm this change replaces
primary.claim: +5-7% over the AVX2 inner, significant in all six cells

secondary_and_more_important.note: The same runs also answer a question this change did not set out to ask: is the default-on owner worth having at all on this host? Ratios below are owner_avxvnni256 vs the SAME sweep's off arm, paired per round.
secondary_and_more_important.reading: On 3B -- the model class the owner's default-on receipt used -- owner_avx2 was LOSING to off on this host (off/avx2 = 1.0396, 1.0336, 1.0188). The new inner flips that: the owner now beats off by 2.5-3.9%. On 1B the owner is break-even at short prompts and still a significant 2.7% LOSS at 2421 tokens even with the new inner. That 1B regression is pre-existing, is NOT fixed here, and is the open question this receipt hands back.

engagement_accounting.counts: 1B: 80 / 240 / 800 for 124 / 606 / 2421 tokens. 3B: 140 / 420 / 1400. Both scale exactly with chunk count.
engagement_accounting.contrast_with_the_kquant_owner: There the new inner covered 6 of 7 owner matmuls because Q4_K_M mixes in a per-layer Q6_K tensor. Here the model is uniformly Q8_0, so the new inner covers 100% of owner matmuls.
engagement_accounting.vnni512_taken: not applicable on this host; the 512-bit arms are not even offered by the capability-aware sweep.

parity.unit: q8_0_owner_avxvnni_microkernel_is_bit_identical compares to_bits() against BOTH q8_0_packed_rows4_gemm4_block_scalar (the oracle) and q8_0_packed_rows4_gemm4_accumulate_block_avx2 (the kernel being replaced). Accumulator seeded non-zero so the += contract is covered. Boundary quants 0, -127, +127 pinned explicitly.
parity.negative_control: Removing the weight-sign fold (`sign_epi8(input, weight)` -> bare broadcast) makes the test FAIL on the scalar-oracle assertion. The test is not vacuous.
parity.why_it_must_be_exact: dpbusd sums four adjacent u8 x i8 products into each i32 lane, which is exactly what maddubs_epi16 + madd_epi16(_, ones) computes, and unlike maddubs it carries no saturating i16 intermediate. Lane-pair to output-lane mapping is unchanged, accumulation is associative i32, and the f32 tail keeps the siblings' (dot * weight_scale) * input_scale order with no FMA.

blast_radius.avx512_hosts: provably unaffected -- use_avxvnni requires !use_vnni, so a host that selects the 512-bit inner never evaluates it. The 4x8 tile is likewise unreachable here because use_4x8 requires use_vnni.
blast_radius.non_avxvnni_hosts: unaffected -- same AVX2/scalar branch as before.
blast_radius.operator_knobs: no new knob. The existing CAMELID_X86_Q8_MATMUL_OWNER_VNNI selects the widest VNNI inner the host can run.
blast_radius.default_state: the Q8 owner is already default-on for windows x86_64 (Q8MatmulOwnerScope::from_env), so this changes which kernel ships, not whether the owner ships.

open_questions: The 1B Q8 regression against off (0.973 at 2421 tokens, 0/8 rounds) is real, pre-existing, and untouched by this change. The owner's default-on receipt was taken on a 3B model on an i7-11800H -- a non-hybrid part -- so neither the small-model case nor the hybrid-core case was covered. Someone should decide whether the owner should be size-gated.
Only one host, and it is hybrid. AVX-VNNI also ships on Alder/Meteor/Arrow Lake and on Zen 5; none measured.
The 4x8 tile has no 256-bit twin. It is AVX-512-only, so AVX-VNNI hosts get the 4x4 tile only -- there may be more left on the table.
Only Llama-architecture Q8_0 models were swept.
verdict: Lands as an additive fast path on a DEFAULT-ON code path: +5-7% prefill over the AVX2 inner in all six measured cells, 57/58 paired rounds, byte-identical output, and no reachable change on any AVX-512 host. On 3B it converts the owner from a measured net loss into a measured net win against off.
